name: Petteri Orpo
party: Kansallinen Kokoomus (KOK, National Coalition Party) — European People's Party (EPP)
bio: Antti Petteri Orpo, born in Köyliö in 1969 and a Master of Social Sciences (valtiotieteiden maisteri) of the University of Turku, has been Prime Minister of Finland since 20 June 2023 and chairman of the National Coalition Party (Kokoomus) since June 2016, when he unseated Alexander Stubb; delegates re-elected him unopposed in June 2026. A Turku-based member of Parliament for Varsinais-Suomi (Finland Proper) since 2007, he was Minister of Agriculture and Forestry (2014–2015), Minister of the Interior (2015–2016) and Minister of Finance (2016–2019, also Deputy Prime Minister from 2017), and briefly Speaker of Parliament in spring 2023. After Kokoomus came first in the April 2023 election with 20.8% of the vote and 48 seats, he formed a four-party right-wing coalition with the Finns Party, the Swedish People's Party and the Christian Democrats. His government has pursued spending cuts and tax changes to curb public debt, a series of labour-market reforms (a cap on political strikes, an export-led wage model, easier dismissals and fixed-term contracts), stricter immigration and citizenship rules and, citing Russia's use of migrants against Finland's eastern border, a temporary law allowing asylum applications to be refused at the border. As of October 2026 its central targets of 100,000 more people in work and a stabilised debt ratio have not been met: unemployment is around 10% and the European Commission has recommended placing Finland under the EU's excessive deficit procedure. In July 2026 he survived a confidence vote (101–90) after the government withdrew a €35 million subsidy for the Garden Helsinki arena, and the Chancellor of Justice is examining complaints about whether he should have recused himself from decisions involving a Kokoomus campaign donor. The next parliamentary election is due in spring 2027.
